questions.question: Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 500 g of water from 20 degrees C to 60 degrees C. Take specific heat capacity of water as 4200 J/kg K.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Given:** $m = 500\ \text{g} = 0.5\ \text{kg},\ c = 4200\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$
$$\Delta T = 60 - 20 = 40\ \text{K}$$

**Step 2 — Heat required:**
$$Q = mc\Delta T = 0.5 \times 4200 \times 40$$
$$Q = 2100 \times 40$$
$$\boxed{Q = \mathbf{8.4 \times 10^4\ \text{J}} = \mathbf{84\ kJ}}$$

**Step 3 — In calories** (using $1\ \text{cal} = 4.2\ \text{J}$):
$$Q = \frac{8.4 \times 10^4}{4.2} = 2.0 \times 10^4\ \text{cal} = 20\ \text{kcal}$$

**Check:** Doubling the mass ($m \propto Q$) while keeping the temperature rise the same doubles the heat needed, which is consistent.
questions.knowledgeNote: Heat needed is mass times specific heat times temperature rise; 0.5 kg water through 40 K needs 84000 joules.
